n01-open
The Diagram Builder isn't only a web app. <break time='150ms'/> Its tools work inside your AI agent.
n02-title
In this episode: GitHub Copilot designs, validates, hardens, prices and exports an architecture, through the Diagram Builder's MCP server.
n03-tools
The MCP server gives an agent thirteen tools: validation and hardening, cost estimates, Bicep and Terraform, diagrams, and import and export.
n03-tools-generic
The MCP server gives an agent the Diagram Builder's tools: validation and hardening, cost estimates, infrastructure as code, diagrams, and import and export.
n04-connect
Connecting takes one entry in your MCP settings and a personal key. <break time='120ms'/> It works in VS Code, in the Copilot CLI, and in any client that supports MCP.
n05-ask
Here's GitHub Copilot in the terminal, with one request: design a clinic booking app, validate it, harden it with a second region, price it, and export it.
n06-validate
Copilot drafts the design and calls the validation tool. It gets back a design score and the gaps to fix.
n07-harden
Then it hardens the design with Central US as the second region, and validates again.
n08-cost
It prices the result with Azure retail prices, and exports the design for the web app.
n09-summary
The summary: the score before and after, the cost, and the settings that are still left for deployment.
n10-open
And the agent's design opens in the web app.
n11-tour
The regions, the services and the connections, with prices and the request flow, ready to refine, review and share.
n12-close
Your architecture tools, wherever you work. <break time='150ms'/> That's AADB Everywhere.
